What

What Large Tree Removal Involves

Large tree removal is the complete takedown of any tree where conventional felling is unsafe — typically 60+ ft in mature canopy, though the threshold drops fast when the tree is near a structure, in tight access, or in declining condition. Roubic's large-tree workflow defaults to crane-assisted dismantling: we set rigging from above, take the tree down in controlled sections, and load directly into the truck rather than dropping wood and re-handling. This compresses on-site time, reduces ground impact, and is the only safe approach for many estate-canopy scenarios.

Crane-assisted removal becomes the default for trees adjacent to structures — houses, garages, fences, pools; trees over 60 ft in tight residential access; trees in declining condition where climber anchorage is unreliable; trees with major lean where directional felling is impossible; trees in or near power line corridors; and multi-tree clusters where ground-handling time would be prohibitive.

Why

Four Reasons NE Ohio Owners Call Roubic

The large-tree scenarios Aaron walks most often across NE Ohio estate and residential properties.

Dead 90-ft Ash Over the House

An EAB-killed ash adjacent to a roofline goes structurally unsafe fast. Crane-assisted takedown before it fails.

Heritage Oak or Maple in Decline

Cavity decay over a roofline. Heritage red oaks, sugar maples, and beeches that have outgrown safe felling.

Storm-Damaged Estate Canopy

A sugar maple with a split crown after a Cleveland storm — sectional dismantling from above, not risky felling.

Tight-Access or Multi-Tree Estate

Village-scale lots and 3-acre estates where ground-handling time would be prohibitive. One crane setup, several trees.

How

Common Large-Tree Questions

Large Tree Removal FAQ

Five things NE Ohio owners want to know before booking a large-tree removal.

What counts as a 'large' tree for removal pricing?
Practically, any tree where conventional felling is unsafe — typically 60+ ft, though the threshold drops fast in tight access or near structures. Crane-assisted dismantling becomes the default for most trees over 80 ft, regardless of access.
How much does large tree removal cost in NE Ohio?
Crane-assisted large-tree removal typically runs $3,500–$15,000 depending on tree size, access, total picks, and crane positioning complexity. Heritage estate trees (Pepper Pike, Moreland Hills) routinely fall in the upper range. See the Tree Service Cost Guide for full benchmarks.
Why does Roubic use a crane instead of just felling the tree?
Crane-assisted removal is safer for the property and faster on-site. We set rigging from above, take the tree down in controlled sections, and load directly into the truck. Conventional felling is unsafe for most large trees in residential access — directional control is too coarse for the tolerances involved.
Do I need a permit for large tree removal?
Permit requirements depend on the village. Pepper Pike, Chagrin Falls, Moreland Hills, Solon, Gates Mills, Beachwood, and Shaker Heights all have tree protection ordinances. Roubic coordinates the permit workflow as part of every removal estimate.
Can Roubic handle multiple large trees in one job?
Yes — multi-tree estate packages are a Roubic specialty. Pricing typically improves on a per-tree basis when crane positioning serves multiple trees from a single setup. Estate properties on Pepper Pike, Moreland Hills, and Gates Mills routinely book multi-tree packages.
